document: LinkedIn framework: Open with a surprising symptom -> diagnose the real cause -> explain why the obvious fix fails -> give 3 practical corrections -> close with a small CTA. Best for expert education and stuck audiences.

LinkedIn framework: Start with an exact customer objection in quotes -> validate the fear -> reframe what the objection is really about -> show one example -> invite comments from people who feel the same.
LinkedIn framework: Before state -> emotional friction -> turning point -> after state -> bridge steps -> CTA. Keep before and after concrete, not vague transformation language.
LinkedIn framework: Name the costly mistake -> show 3 ways it appears -> explain the hidden cost of each -> give the better replacement -> CTA to save or comment.
LinkedIn framework: Specific personal scene -> tension or embarrassment -> decision made -> lesson learned -> how the reader can apply it -> CTA. Use sensory or situational detail early.
LinkedIn framework: State the myth -> why it sounds believable -> evidence or repeated observation against it -> better belief -> first action. Use for belief-change posts.
LinkedIn framework: When to use this checklist -> 5-7 checks -> one priority check explained deeper -> warning sign -> CTA to save for the next decision.
LinkedIn framework: Common advice -> who it hurts -> hidden tradeoff -> better principle -> example from the creator or audience -> soft CTA.
LinkedIn framework: Show the old method -> where it breaks -> introduce the new method -> break it into named steps -> show what improves. Good for authority building.
LinkedIn framework: One ordinary day moment -> what outsiders do not see -> why it matters for results -> one lesson -> CTA. Good for service businesses and creators.
LinkedIn framework: Pattern seen across clients/customers -> example without private details -> why the pattern happens -> what to try instead -> CTA.
LinkedIn framework: Name a simple model -> explain each part in short sections -> show a use case -> identify who should use it -> CTA for template or comment.
LinkedIn framework: List failed alternatives the audience has tried -> explain why each feels reasonable -> reveal the missing piece -> offer a simpler next step.
LinkedIn framework: Predict a change in the niche -> explain current signal -> show risk of ignoring it -> give preparation steps -> invite opinions.
LinkedIn framework: Why the creator started -> what problem kept repeating -> how the offer/method formed -> who it is for now -> CTA.
LinkedIn framework: Mini case context -> constraint -> action taken -> result -> what others can copy -> CTA. Keep numbers or observable outcomes specific.
LinkedIn framework: Open with a high-intent question -> short answer -> nuanced answer -> example -> what to do next. Good for SEO-style LinkedIn posts.
LinkedIn framework: Name the situation -> list red flags -> explain the highest-risk one -> safer alternative -> CTA to save/share.
LinkedIn framework: Unpopular truth -> why people resist it -> what changes after accepting it -> practical example -> CTA for discussion.
LinkedIn framework: Story hook -> 3 chronological steps -> mistake or surprise at each step -> final lesson -> CTA. Blends story with practical instruction.
Instagram carousel framework: Slide 1 problem hook -> slide 2 why it happens -> slides 3-6 step-by-step fix -> slide 7 example -> slide 8 save/share CTA.
Instagram carousel framework: Slide 1 “Stop doing this” hook -> slides 2-5 mistakes -> slides 6-8 fixes -> slide 9 quick recap -> slide 10 save CTA.
Instagram carousel framework: Slide 1 myth statement -> slides 2-3 why people believe it -> slides 4-7 truth and proof -> final slide “share with someone who needs this.”
Instagram carousel framework: Slide 1 outcome promise -> slides 2-8 one checklist item per slide -> final slide when to use it and save CTA.
Instagram carousel framework: Slide 1 quote the objection -> slides 2-4 validate and unpack it -> slides 5-8 reframe with examples -> final slide comment or DM CTA.
Instagram carousel framework: Slide 1 before/after contrast -> slides 2-3 before details -> slides 4-6 bridge actions -> slides 7-8 after signs -> final CTA.
Instagram carousel framework: Slide 1 personal confession -> slides 2-4 what happened -> slides 5-7 lesson -> final slide “if this is you, start here.”
Instagram story framework: Story 1 relatable problem -> story 2 poll -> story 3 quick tip -> story 4 example/proof -> story 5 DM keyword CTA.
Instagram story framework: Story 1 quiz myth/truth -> story 2 reveal -> story 3 explain why -> story 4 ask if they want a checklist -> story 5 DM keyword.
Instagram story framework: Story 1 morning/context -> stories 2-4 behind-the-scenes moments -> story 5 lesson -> story 6 question sticker.
Instagram story framework: Story 1 anonymous client/customer starting point -> story 2 obstacle -> story 3 action -> story 4 result -> story 5 reply prompt.
Instagram story framework: Story 1 ask for objections/questions -> story 2 answer one objection -> story 3 proof -> story 4 soft offer or DM CTA.
Instagram story framework: Story 1 this-or-that choice -> story 2 explain better choice -> story 3 quick example -> story 4 saveable summary screenshot.
Instagram Reel framework: 0-2s visual hook -> 3-8s show the mistake/result -> 9-20s demonstrate fix -> 21-28s recap -> caption CTA.
Instagram Reel framework: POV text hook -> show familiar frustrating moment -> cut to better way -> add 3 caption beats -> CTA to follow/save.
Instagram Reel framework: Fast hook -> count 3 mistakes with quick examples -> show replacement for each -> end with save CTA.
Instagram Reel framework: Show before visual or phrase -> transition to after -> overlay the 3 bridge steps -> caption adds detail -> CTA.
Instagram Reel framework: Behind-the-scenes process clips -> overlay why each step matters -> reveal final result -> caption teaches one lesson.
Instagram Reel framework: Use a comment/question as the hook -> answer directly -> show example -> invite more questions in comments.
Instagram Reel framework: “I used to think…” hook -> one personal detail -> what changed -> one practical lesson -> CTA to share with a friend.
Length rule: Short posts should make one point only: hook -> 1 insight -> 1 example or proof -> CTA. Avoid multiple sections.
Length rule: Medium posts can include hook -> context -> 2-3 teaching points -> example -> CTA. This is the default for most useful posts.
Length rule: Long posts should earn the extra length with narrative, proof, nuance, and a clear structure. Use sections, but keep paragraphs short.
